extracted.intended_audience: Peer reviewers (academic researchers) invited to review for Frontiers journals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for academic reviewers on how to conduct peer review within Frontiers' single-anonymized, interactive review model, including pre-invitation checks, conduct during independent and interactive phases, reporting expectations, timing, conflicts of interest, and post-review recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review model — single anonymized
rubrics_metrics.description: Frontiers operates a single anonymized model during the review process where reviewers know who the authors are.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers know authors to offer a full assessment within the context of their research and to ensure potential competing interests can be avoided. Frontiers discloses the name of all endorsing reviewers upon publication for every article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent review phase — assess independently
rubrics_metrics.description: During the first review phase, reviewers assess the paper independently from each other and the authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After accepting the invitation, reviewers access the review forum, review the manuscript and supporting documents, complete a tailored review questionnaire, and submit a recommendation to the editor. Reviewers may directly endorse the manuscript if it meets acceptance criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of tailored review questionnaire
rubrics_metrics.description: The review is completed by answering a review questionnaire provided in the review forum, tailored for each article type (original research, review, study protocol, clinical trial, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make good use of the detailed questionnaire to provide a clear assessment; it helps structure comments and ensures key evaluation points are covered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling editor role between phases
rubrics_metrics.description: Once all reviewers have submitted reports, the handling editor reviews report comments before activating the interactive review phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The handling editor is responsible for reviewing reports and then enabling the collaborative forum where authors can rebut and respond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interactive review phase — author response and dialogue
rubrics_metrics.description: Once activated, authors can view and respond to reviewers' comments in the review forum; reviewers are notified when authors reply or resubmit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers can enter a dialog with authors to request clarifications or further revisions, access and comment on other reviewers' reports, and decide to endorse or recommend rejection based on revisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Before accepting — expertise fit
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the manuscript is suitably within your area of expertise before accepting the invitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the manuscript is outside your expertise, decline and consider suggesting alternative relevant experts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Before accepting — time availability and turnaround
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider whether you have the time to complete the review; reviewers are requested to complete reports within seven days after accepting the invite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If seven days is insufficient or delays arise after acceptance, contact the editorial office to request an extension or assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Before accepting — conflicts of interest disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete the short questionnaire regarding conflicts of interest once the invitation is accepted to establish any relationship with the author(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conflicts are assessed case by case and may not be disqualifying; disclose all answers in full. Further details are provided by the journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respond to invitation promptly
rubrics_metrics.description: Respond to the review invitation as soon as you can and decline if you lack time or expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When declining, recommendations for alternative reviewers are appreciated. If you need to request an extension or will be delayed after accepting, notify the editorial office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on quality of the science objectively
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim to focus on the quality of the science in an objective manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even though reviewer sees author names, assess only the manuscript, not the author. Concentrate on scientific content, rigor, and validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborate towards improvement and constructive tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Collaborate with authors and editors to improve the manuscript, thinking constructively when providing feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide comments that recommend reasonable improvements, use a polite and impersonal tone, and show professional courtesy by imagining what you'd want to receive on your own paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Help author and editor understand needed changes with clear comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Help the author and handling editor understand what is needed through clear comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide precise, detailed feedback and explain recommendations and decisions; conclude reports with clear recommendations for the handling editor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect the manuscript's stated scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep the focus on what the manuscript is aiming to do, as explained in the authors' 'contribution to the field' statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid recommending that authors vastly expand the scope of the manuscript or take them outside their intended scope (e.g., telling them to address unrelated topics).

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on science rather than minor copy-editing
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should focus on research content; it is not necessary to flag small copy-editing errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The production team will fix minor copy-editing issues during typesetting; prioritize scientific issues, methodology, interpretation, and clarity of contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide constructive positive feedback when deserved
rubrics_metrics.description: If the manuscript is good, tell the authors and explain why.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balanced reviews should note strengths as well as weaknesses—praise with explanation helps authors and editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider field-specific elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply your expertise to give feedback on elements of the research specific to your field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Field-specific insight will be helpful to authors and other reviewers; point out domain-relevant strengths or concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid being vague or too brief
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide precise and detailed feedback rather than short, vague reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Brief reports often generate additional questions and slow the process. Use the detailed questionnaire to ensure clarity and completeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include key points in the initial report
rubrics_metrics.description: The initial report should be thorough and include all necessary feedback and key points upfront.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While revisions may raise new questions, ensure your initial report contains the main concerns; end with a clear recommendation for the handling editor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not drop out of the review process
rubrics_metrics.description: Try to submit responses on time and avoid withdrawing mid-process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you need to request an extension or withdraw, do so via the review forum or contact the editorial office; be mindful of authors anxiously awaiting feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep in touch with the journal office for issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Contact the journal's office if you encounter issues, need assistance using the platform, or need to request an extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The editorial office can assist with platform problems, deadline extensions, or other concerns during review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition policy for reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers who endorse a manuscript for publication are named on the published article; reviewers who recommend rejection or withdraw are not published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a report is submitted, reviewers receive a confirmation email acknowledging their work and including a copy of their report. The report itself is not to be shared publicly, but the confirmation can be used to obtain recognition with institutions or platforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial quality checks before peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Before a manuscript is sent for peer review, the research integrity team and the handling editor conduct initial quality checks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These checks help ensure that submissions meet baseline standards before engaging external reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review recommendation options and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: When submitting a report, reviewers must include their recommendation to the handling editor (endorse, request revisions, or recommend rejection).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure your recommendation is supported by the report's reasoning and that you make clear whether you would endorse the manuscript after revisions or consider it unsuitable for publication.
